extracted.intended_audience: users/developers of SINGULAR (computational algebra) libraries working with tropical/Groebner fans and hyperplane arrangements
extracted.subtask_description: Reference documentation for SINGULAR library procedures in tropical.lib and arr.lib: describes usage, assumptions, return values, notes and examples for computing tropical/Groebner fans and manipulating hyperplane arrangements.

rubrics_metrics.name: tropicalVariety
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: tropicalVariety(f[,p]); f poly, p optional number OR tropicalVariety(I[,p]); I ideal, p optional number. Assume: I homogeneous, p prime number. Return: fan, the tropical variety of f resp. I with respect to the trivial valuation or the p-adic valuation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Note: set printlevel=1 for output during traversal. Example shows calls LIB "tropical.lib"; ring and ideal definitions and tropicalVariety(I) producing a PolyhedralFan structure; can pass a number(p) to compute p-adic variant.

rubrics_metrics.name: groebnerFan
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: groebnerFan(f); f poly OR groebnerFan(I); I ideal. Assume: I homogeneous. Return: fan, the Groebner fan of f resp. I.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Note: set printlevel=1 for output during traversal. Example demonstrates calling groebnerFan(I) and inspecting the returned PolyhedralFan fields (AMBIENT_DIM, DIM, RAYS, CONES, MAXIMAL_CONES, etc.).

rubrics_metrics.name: groebnerComplex
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: groebnerComplex(f,p); f poly, p number OR groebnerComplex(I,p); I ideal, p number. Assume: I homogeneous, p prime number. Return: fan, the Groebner complex of f resp. I with respect to the p-adic valuation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Note: set printlevel=1 for output during traversal. Examples show groebnerComplex(I,number(2)) and variations with different p, producing PolyhedralFan output with detailed combinatorial data.

rubrics_metrics.name: arrSet
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: arrSet(A, k, p); arr A, int k, poly p. Return: [arr] Arrangement where the k-th hyperplane is replaced by p.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Note: p must be linear. Example: arrSet(A,1,x+1) replaces first hyperplane.

rubrics_metrics.name: type2arr
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: type2arr(#); # def. Return: [arr] Arrangement defined by the input.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The procedure tries to cast the input to [arr] using arrAdd. Example shows typeof(type2arr(I)) returns arr for an ideal I.

rubrics_metrics.name: mat2arr
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: mat2arr(M); matrix (M|b). Return: [arr] interprets the rows of the matrix as the defining polynomial equations of the arrangement where the last column will be considered as the constant terms.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If M is m*(n+1) the i-th row defines H_i = Ker(M_i1*x1 + ... + M_in*xn + M_i(n+1)). Example prints resulting arrangement polynomials.

rubrics_metrics.name: mat2carr
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: mat2carr(M); matrix M. Return: [arr] interprets the rows of the matrix as the defining polynomial equations of the arrangement (no constant column).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If M is m*n then H_i = Ker(M_i1*x1 + ... + M_in*xn). Example demonstrates conversion of 4x3 matrix to an arrangement of 4 hyperplanes.

rubrics_metrics.name: arrPrintMatrix
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: arrPrintMatrix(arr A). Return: prints arr in matrix form.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Note: differs from print(matrix(arr A)) since variables are included in output. Example shows matrix-style printout with coefficients and constants.

rubrics_metrics.name: varMat
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: varMat(v); v intvec. Return: [matrix] M containing the corresponding ring variables.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: with ring variables x(1..6) and v = 2,4,6 returns matrix with x(2), x(4), x(6). See related procedures arrLastVar, arrSwapVar, varNum.

rubrics_metrics.name: varNum
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: varnum(string s) OR varnum(ring variable). Return: [int] number of given ring variable, or 0 if it does not appear.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Note: same functionality as varNum from dmod.lib but also accepts polys as input. Example: varNum(y) -> 2; varNum("y(3)") -> numeric index.

rubrics_metrics.name: arrSwapVar
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: arrSwapVar(A, i, j); arr A, ring variables/integers i,j. Return: [arr] A where variables i and j are swapped.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Note: if i and/or j are integers the algorithm uses variables(A)[i] and/or variables(A)[j]. Example shows swapping variables and resulting arrangement.

rubrics_metrics.name: arrLastVar
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: arrLastVar(A); arr A. Return: [int] number of the last variable A uses.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Useful to get full list x1...xk used in A without skipping variables as variables(A) might. Example demonstrates varMat(1..n) after arrLastVar.

rubrics_metrics.name: arrCenter
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: arrCenter(A); arr A. Return: [list] L: entry 0 signals if A not centered, otherwise entries [1, x, H], where x is a particular point of the center and H is a matrix consisting of vectors spanning the linear intersection space. If unique solution then H = 0.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The intersection of all hyperplanes is expressed as linear system Ax=b solved via LU decomposition. Examples show outputs for centerless, single-point center, and line-center cases.

rubrics_metrics.name: arrCentral
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: arrCentral(A); arr A. Return: [0,1] true if arr is central (i.e. all planes intersect in 0).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Note: this is the same as homog(A). Examples show relations between centered/central.

rubrics_metrics.name: arrCentered
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: arrCentered(A); arr A. Return: [0,1] true if A is centered (i.e. intersection of all planes not empty).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Note: algorithm uses ranks: Ax=b has a solution iff rank(A) = rank(A|b). Examples illustrate centered/centerless arrays.

rubrics_metrics.name: arrCentralize
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: arrCentralize(A); arr A. Return: [arr] A after centralization via coordinate change.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Note: coordinate change only performs translation; the translation vector is the second output of arrCenter. Example shows how hyperplanes are translated.

rubrics_metrics.name: arrCoordChange
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: arrCoordChange(A, T) OR arrCoordChange(A, T, c) OR arrCoordChange(A, T_with_last_column); arr A, matrix T (n*n or n*n+1) and optional c. Return: [arr] Arrangement [A|b] after coordinate change f: x -> T x + c with T invertible; formula [A|b] => [A T^-1 | b + A T^-1 c].
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Three input options: nxn matrix (auto-completes T), nxn matrix and nx1 vector c (auto-completes), or nx(n+1) matrix using last column as c. Examples: lift plane, swap variables, swap+translate.

rubrics_metrics.name: arrCoordNormalize
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: arrCoordNormalize(A, v); Return: [arr] Arrangement after a coordinate change transforming A so that (AT^-1) v = I and (b + AT^-1 c) v = 0.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Algorithm does a base change if H_k is homogeneous and an affine transformation otherwise. The goal is to normalize A with respect to index vector v. Example demonstrates reordering/normalizing hyperplanes.

rubrics_metrics.name: arrCone
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: arrCone(A) OR arrCone(A, ring_variable); arr A arrangement in variables x1...xn. Return: arr, the coned hyperplane arrangement cA with respect to the given ring variable (or last variable if none given).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Hyperplanes are homogenized w.r.t. the chosen variable and a new hyperplane H = ker(x_{n+1}) is added. Example shows homogenization and insertion of new variable/hyperplane.

rubrics_metrics.name: arrDecone
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: arrDecone(A, k); arrangement A, integer k. Return: arr: the deconed hyperplane arrangement dA.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A must be non-empty and central. arrDecone is inverse to arrCone: A == arrDecone(arrCone(A),size(A)+1). To decone with respect to arbitrary hyperplane k, a coordinate change is necessary (use arrCoordChange). Example shows deconing a central arrangement.

rubrics_metrics.name: arrLocalize
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: arrLocalize(A, v); arrangement A, intvec v. Return: arr: the localized arrangement A_X containing only hyperplanes which contain the flat X defined by equations A[v].
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example uses arrTypeB(3) and selects a localization by indices; see related arrRestrict/arrEssentialize functions.

rubrics_metrics.name: arrRestrict
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: arrRestrict(A, v) OR arrRestrict(A, k) OR arrRestrict(A, v, "CC"); Return: arr: the restricted hyperplane arrangement (A^X) to the flat X defined by A[v] (or by single index k).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Note: A must be non-empty. Restriction performed only if ideal defining X is monomial (i.e. X is an intersection of coordinate planes). If optional argument "CC" given, arrangement is transformed so X has that coordinate form. Examples illustrate different usages including vector of indices.

rubrics_metrics.name: arrIsEssential
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: arrIsEssential(A); arrangement A. Return: boolean: 1 if arr is essential, i.e. rank of maximal element of poset equals dimension.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Note: A must be non-empty. Examples show check on simple arrangements.

rubrics_metrics.name: arrEssentialize
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: arrEssentialize(A); arrangement A. Return: essential arrangement by transformation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Note: A must be non-empty. Example shows transforming braid and other arrangements to essential form.

rubrics_metrics.name: arrBoolean
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: arrBoolean(v); int v. Return: arr which uses the first v variables of ring for boolean arrangement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: arrBoolean(7) returns arrangement consisting of x(1),...,x(7). See related arrTypeB, arrBraid functions.

rubrics_metrics.name: arrBraid
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: arrBraid(v); int v. Return: Type A (braid) arrangement of dimension v.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Entry labeled as returning the standard braid arrangement (type A) for given dimension; example section continues beyond provided chunk.
